text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Inflation in Bulgaria for the first 11 months of 1996 is expected to top 200 percent, National Statistics Institute preliminary figures showed.

-- Bulgaria's Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov is expected to lift all bans on meat and livestock transport because no new cases of foot-and-mouth disease were reported in the country after an outbreak of the disease in Southeastern Bulgaria was eliminated.
-- Currency deposits of individuals in Bulgarian commercial banks fell to 1.325 billion at the end of November from $2.122 billion at the beginning of 1996, preliminary central bank figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet should open tender procedures for the sell-off of at least 50 percent of Bulgaria's state magnetic storage device producer DZU Stara Zagora, a DZU senior official said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions (CITU) said it expected some one million Bulgarians to join a 24-hour strike planned for December 4 to demand a cabinet reshuffle and early parliamentary elections.

-- Russia's private companies Rif and Elit are seen as the most serious candidates for buying a stake in Bulgaria's state forklift truck producer Balkankar holding, Bulgaria's Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) could restore confidence in the lev without introducing a currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund if it comes to power, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected next week to start technical consultations on the introduction of a currency board system with an International Monetary Fund mission, Deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim is expected to propose to the government to raise fuel prices by 34.6 percent to compensate refinery's losses due to the sharp fall of the lev against the dollar in the last three weeks, the newspaper said without qouting sources.
